summary: Independent review of T46 (auto-fetch floor surface coverage). The 18-row widening is sound and correctly closed at all four boundaries, the deferred set is exactly what the documents claim, and all nine prior matrices plus the benign corpus reproduce their recorded outcomes. Two blockers: both gates T46 introduced (input type=image, meta http-equiv=refresh) compare the RAW attribute value while a renderer compares the decoded one, so 7 character-reference spellings of two DECLARED-COVERED surfaces reach a client with redaction.state=none at mcp/persist/transport/seam; and three CommonMark reference-image spellings (collapsed, shortcut, balanced-bracket description) that neither enumeration found are released, while the re-derivation and the edited requirements package assert that surface is completely covered. Ruling on the flagged judgement call: keep <iframe src> covered. The eager rows are acceptable but their disclosure understates the case-insensitive false-positive class. The normative edit was warranted but is inaccurate in both directions. A concurrent writer replaced exfil.ts and exfil.test.ts mid-review (T62#F-001 <base> suppression revert); every probe re-run after the drift is byte-identical, but T46's verification no longer describes the tree.

findings.problem: Both gates T46 introduced (`<input>` requires type=image at :845, `<meta>` requires http-equiv=refresh at :848) compare the RAW attribute value. The HTML tokenizer consumes character references in attribute-value states, so http-equiv="refresh" IS refresh and type="image" IS an image submit button. The module asserts that premise twice itself (renderableUrl, and metaRefreshDestination which decodes `content` for exactly this reason) and withholds it from the two gates.
findings.impact: 7 measured spellings of two surfaces the requirements package declares covered reach a model client unmasked, including the NAV surface that navigates the whole client to the attacker. All 7 return isError:false with redaction.state="none" and pass prepareOutputForPersistence, validateOutputForTransport and the seam byte-identical with attacker.invalid present. Spelling bypass of a covered surface (AC5) and a failure of 'every covered surface is closed at the tool dispatch and the persistence materializer'.

All three render an auto-fetching . T46 declared the enumeration re-derived from the standard, listed the markdown reference definition as covered, and wrote that completeness into the requirements package as 'перечень полный, не пример'.
findings.impact: The most ordinary markdown reference-image spelling — ![logo] with [logo]: URL at the bottom of a README — is a zero-click exfil channel the mandatory floor releases, reaching mcp/persist/transport/seam with redaction.state="none". The detector gap predates T46; the false completeness claim in a normative document does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the second bracket group optional and empty-tolerant, resolving the label to the second group when non-empty and to the description otherwise (CommonMark's collapsed/shortcut rule), keeping the existing '!'-only gate so plain reference links stay click-gated; fix INLINE's description grammar separately; then correct T46-spec 2.1 and the policies.md covered list.

The background attribute is current practice in HTML email templates for Outlook, and such a template is a FILE-shaped carrier with no particular content — the property T46 used to defer script and link.

findings.problem: 'Masking it removes a navigation nobody wanted, so the mask has no cost of its own' is true of a rendered document and false of a quoted one. A generated documentation redirect stub is a file whose entire content is one <meta http-equiv=refresh>, and the whole directive is the mask span, so a reader of that file loses both the destination and the timeout.
findings.impact: Small and does not change the decision (the NAV blast radius dominates), but the cost weighing records a zero where there is not one.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the redirect-stub carrier in section 6 beside the <iframe> disclosure.

findings.problem: U17 moved from 'cover now' to 'never cover' on the claim that a <frame> start tag is ignored in the 'in body' insertion mode. That is a tree-builder claim no oracle in this flow can test — lol-html attributes src to <frame> exactly as to <iframe> — and the spec's in-body rules do not name frame, so it falls to 'any other start tag'. The stated reason for choosing never over cover is aesthetic.
findings.impact: An asymmetric bet: if the claim holds, covering costs one table entry and zero measured false positives; if it fails in any renderer, the surface stays open and a regression test now pins it open.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add frame: { src: EMBEDDED_URL } to FETCHING_ATTRIBUTES and the element to HTML_START_TAG, or downgrade the recorded reason to 'not measured; excluded on the spec reading of the in-body insertion mode'.
